findings.reason: Confirmed. Abe's Theorem 4.2.2 (arXiv 1310.0528v3, §4.2.1–4.2.2, pp. 103–104) is stated for A_r, the cuspidal representations of GL_r(A_F) 'with central character of finite order', and I_r, the isocrystals with determinant of finite order. The accepted PAPER-ABE-18/32 records exactly this, and PAPER-ABE-18 route 2's brief states the final theorem 'with finite central character'. PAPER-DADDEZIO-23 route 4's brief instead says D'Addezio 'consumes Abe's Theorem 4.2.2 exactly as that brief states it: every Q̄_p-linear cuspidal automorphic representation ... corresponds', and 'It adds no target'. Item 19 also says 'every'. The consumer, Theorem 5.3.3 (item 68), is stated for every cuspidal π with no central-character hypothesis. So the twisting reduction is needed and is planned nowhere. Over a function field every idele class character is a finite-order character times an unramified degree character c^{deg}, so the reduction is short, but it needs the matching rank-one constant F-isocrystal on the other side and the slope shift by v_p(c) in the minimal-slope Hecke eigenvalues. The fix is right. Medium is right: one consumer theorem, a short reduction.

Confirmed. Item 1 is 'planned' at PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3 and is in none of the six routes. RD.3's text plans frames, overconvergent isocrystals with Frobenius pullback isomorphisms, independence of embeddings and restriction to convergent isocrystals. It does not plan the crystalline description Isoc(X) = Crys(X)[1/p], the equivalence with convergent F^n-isocrystals ([Ked22, Thm. 2.2]), or the 2-colimit F^∞-Isoc(X). Item 1's own note says so ('is not named there', 'this paper's construction'). Those parts are therefore unrouted although later items (Λ_η, the exact sequences of Proposition 3.2.8) depend on them. The misprint is real too: p. 6 defines Φ^m_M := Φ_M ∘ F^*(Φ^{m−1}_M) for an F^n-structure Φ_M : (F^n)^*M ≅ M. For n > 1, F^*(Φ^{m−1}_M) has source F^*(F^{n(m−1)})^*M and target F^*M, which is not the source (F^n)^*M of Φ_M. The pullback must be (F^n)^*. This is not among E1–E14 (E1 is a different misprint on the same page). The fix is right; record the misprint as a new sourceIssue (misprint, affects nothing).

Confirmed. On p. 6 the paper defines ω_η : Isoc(X) → Vec_{K(Ω)} and G(M, η) as 'the Tannaka group of ⟨M⟩ with respect to ω_η', so G(M, η) is a group scheme over K(Ω). §3.1 (p. 7) sets K := K(k), and Definition 3.1.2 asks V_M ⊗_{Q_p^ur} K(Ω) = ω_η(M). Yet Proposition 3.3.2 (p. 10) concludes 'G(M, η) ≃ G(M, V_M, η) ⊗_{Q_p^ur} K' and Corollary 4.3.6 (p. 19) 'G(M, η) = G(M†, η) ∩ G(M, Φ^∞_M, η) ⊗_{Q_p^ur} K'. The categorical statement 'Isoc_{Q_p^ur}(X, η)_F ⊗ K → Isoc(X)_F is an equivalence' is right with K = K(k), because Isoc(X) is K(k)-linear. But the group identity then follows only after base change to K(Ω), since V_M ⊗ K(Ω) = ω_η(M) is the fibre functor. Items 42 and 50 and route 6's layer (2) copy '⊗ K'. The red team's unit-object example (Ω strictly bigger than k) shows the printed isomorphism cannot hold over K(k). E2 corrects only the dual fibre in Lemma 3.1.3, and E8 repeats '⊗ K'. The fix is right. It should also record one new sourceIssue covering Proposition 3.3.2 and Corollary 4.3.6 (error, affects a stated result), and note on E8 that its '⊗ K' is also ⊗ K(Ω). The correction is a change of base field, and nothing in the paper's argument depends on the wrong field. But as items 42 and 50 stand, they state isomorphisms of groups over different fields, so I agree they must be fixed before a blueprint uses them.

Confirmed. PAPER-DADDEZIO-23 route 6's reason says 'No layer or proposal plans Crew's monodromy groups of F-isocrystals'. But the accepted PAPER-ABE-18/25, on route 1 (PadicDifferentialEquationsPartIIArithmeticDModules), defines π_1^isoc(X, x̄) := Aut^⊗(ω_x̄) with Isoc^†(X/K̄) ≅ Rep(π_1^isoc), and the Weil group W^isoc (Abe §§2.4.17–2.4.20, pp. 86–88). Its note reads 'Crew's monodromy groups in the Weil-group form Lafforgue uses', and that route's brief lists 'Weil groups of isocrystals'. Restricting to the tensor subcategory generated by M† gives D'Addezio's G(M†, η) (item 33). The overlap is partial: D'Addezio also needs the convergent groups G(M, η), perfect points and K(Ω)-valued fibres. So the right fix is the coordination the finding asks for: a shared prefix with one owner and a comparison, not a merger. Medium is right.
